answers.explanation: unistd.h defines read() and the ssize_t and size_t types.
A file descriptor is the small number the OS gave back when the file was opened.
read() may read fewer bytes, but never more than count.
Zero bytes read means there's nothing left.
It reads what's there, up to count, and returns how many bytes it actually read.
man read shows the manual page.
The API hides that. The programmer only needs the function's parameters and return values.
